To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The liver is capable of eliciting a regional lymph node response to semi-allogeneic liver cells in the F1 hybrid host, which is both dose and time‐dependent.”
the liver is an immunologically active organ and that it is capable of eliciting an immune response in the host.
the liver cells prepared from adult rats are immunogenic, the immunogenicity being both dose and time‐dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the liver in immune response.
the role of liver cells in immune reactions.
the immunological properties of the adult liver cells, the role of the lymphatic system in this phenomenon and the mechanism underlying the liver lymph node response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the liver is an organ which can stimulate a regional lymph node response in the recipient rat when injected into it, and that the liver cells from the fetus, 70% hepatocellular and portacaval shunt animals can also do so.
the liver cells are immunogenic, and the regional lymph node response is the result of a cell mediated reaction, possibly a graft‐versus‐host reaction.
the liver cells are antigenically reactive and that this is a manifestation of the immunological competence of the liver cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
liver cells are potent immunogens and that they are capable of stimulating both the humoral as well as the cellular immune responses.
the liver is a potent antigenic organ and that the liver cells, particularly those prepared from portacaval shunt rats, are the most potent antigenic cells known.
the adult rat liver cells, in addition to their well-known functions, can also be considered as immunological cells which are capable of inducing regional lymph node response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
liver cells are immunogenic.
the liver is a potent immunogen and that the liver‐derived antigen is present in the liver of the newborn rat.
liver transplantation in rats is a feasible procedure, and that it can be accomplished by a simple and reproducible technique.
